title: Scan four groceries across a checkout scanner, one read each, and put them on the bagging shelf
instruction: Ring up the four groceries on the scanner, each item read once, and put them on the bagging shelf.
context: Cashiers (O*NET 41-2011.00; 3.1 million US jobs, 2025) "Establish or identify prices of goods, services, or admission, and tabulate bills, using calculators, cash registers, or optical price scanners". At a presentation scanner such as Zebra's DS9308 (USD 410 with its USB cable) each item is presented with its barcode toward the window and no finger over it; the scanner beeps and its solid green LED goes out once per read, and once the barcode has been out of view for 0.5 s (its default same-symbol timeout) presenting it again rings the item up again. An item bagged unread leaves unpaid. Here every barcode starts facing away from the scanner, and the belt and the bagging shelf are farther apart than one arm reaches, so items go from hand to hand across the counter.
setup: A checkout counter (the table top) in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the counter. (1) Scanner, fixed to the counter in Zebra's locking-mount bracket: a Zebra DS9308-SR hands-free presentation scanner (USB kit DS9308-SR4U2100AZW, USD 410.19 at Barcode Factory on 17 Nov 2026), 14.5 cm tall, 8.6 cm wide, 8.3 cm deep, 318 g, upright, its oval base centred at x 37.3, y 15; its window (about 6.4 x 5 cm) on the head's front face at x 33.5, its middle 10 cm above the counter at y 15, facing the robot; its LED on the head's top, solid green when ready and out for 0.5 s after each read. (2) Belt end, fixed: black rubber flush with the counter, x 2 to 40, y 45.5 to 64.5. (3) Groceries, loose, on the belt, each with a 12-digit UPC-A barcode (100 % size, bars upright) on one side, none facing the scanner: a 1 lb spaghetti box (26.4 x 7.1 x 4.1 cm, 0.48 kg) lying along x at (20, 49), its code on its left face 7 cm from its middle away from the robot; a 10.75 oz can of condensed soup (6.8 x 10.2 cm, 0.35 kg) standing at (4.5, 60.5), code facing back toward the robot; a 16 oz glass jar of salsa (7.5 x 12.7 cm, 0.65 kg) at (15, 60.5), code facing left; a 16.9 fl oz bottle of water (6.5 x 20.4 cm, 0.52 kg) at (26, 60.5), code facing left. (4) Bagging shelf, fixed: brushed stainless flush with the counter, x -5 to 40, y -64.5 to -46, its inner edge marked by a yellow line. The right gripper reaches no further left than y 45 and the left gripper no further right than y -45. Both arms start at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Every control step (20 Hz) the task file reads each grocery's pose and both arms' joints. A code is read when its centre is inside the scanner's 52 x 33 degree field of view (opening toward the robot from the window's middle) 0 to 22.4 cm in front of the window, it faces the window within 60 degrees, it moves slower than 3.05 m/s, and no part of either arm (links, gripper, fingers) lies between the window's middle and any of nine points over the code; the LED then goes out for 0.5 s. After a read the same code reads again only once it has been out of view for 0.5 s (the scanner's default). Score: 0 for the rest of the run once the glass jar falls faster than 1 m/s (dropped about 5 cm) or tumbles faster than 5 rad/s (knocked over), or any grocery falls off the counter. Otherwise 0.25 per item checked out: read exactly once and ending on the bagging shelf (its whole footprint past the yellow line, resting on the shelf, moved less than 3 mm in the last 1 s, every finger 2 cm or more from it). An item read but left on the counter, or read twice or more, earns nothing; an item that reaches the shelf before its first read scores 0 for the rest of the run (it left unpaid). Full score (1.0, success): all four checked out, held for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: the scanner's beeps and its decode log on a PC (or Zebra's 123Scan) give each item's reads; a photo of the shelf gives the bagged items; the videos show a drop.
reset_notes: Stand or lay the four groceries back on their taped marks on the belt with their barcodes turned as in the screenshot; clear the decode log. Nothing is consumed. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX), 20 Hz; everything at true size. The scanner is not simulated optically: a read is computed from the code's pose with the DS9308's field of view, range, skew and pitch tolerance and swipe speed, a line-of-sight test past the arms and its 0.5 s same-symbol timeout. The bars are drawn at true size but not decoded during the run (OpenCV decodes the drawn labels). The LED is modelled, the beep is not. Labels are visual only. No third-party assets.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (the left gripper closed on the water bottle's cap four times but never carried it away; the right arm stayed near its base; nothing was read and nothing reached the shelf); demo: 1.0
